heroHeadline: Cross-Border Strikes Pause After Amzan Tanker Attack, But Taiz Front Fighting Continues
heroSubtitle: A week after a Houthi ballistic missile struck the Saudi VLCC Amzan off Yanbu (Aug 24), the highest-profile Houthi-Saudi exchange — strikes on Saudi soil, oil infrastructure and Red Sea shipping — has gone quiet for the first time since the escalation began. Fighting has not stopped, however: Yemeni Armed Forces say they repelled a Houthi ground assault on Taiz's Kalabah front on Aug 26, killing 8 Houthi fighters and wounding 15 in an unconfirmed, one-sided claim. Brent crude touched a one-month high near $94/bbl by Sep 1 on the broader run of Middle East strikes. UN Special Envoy Hans Grundberg's warning that Yemen faces its highest risk of renewed large-scale war since the April 2022 truce remains unresolved, even as the acute cross-border phase that peaked in mid-to-late August has, for now, eased.
footerNote: Data sourced from Saudi Press Agency, Al Jazeera, Reuters, AP, Washington Post, Bloomberg, NBC News, CNN, NPR, ABC News (Australia), TASS, Türkiye Today, Anadolu Agency, News.Az, Yemen Monitor, Arab News, UN OCHA, UN News, Security Council Report, CFR Global Conflict Tracker, Trading Economics, and the US Senate Armed Services Committee record. Contested claims flagged with opposing perspectives.
